title: Heavy-tier harness 5/5: scripted clean-main baseline (npm run test:baseline) + docs + final census
description:
Piece 5 of LIN-4219's approved plan: a scripted clean-`main` baseline, plus the parent's docs and the final census check. **Blocked by pieces 1 and 2** (the plan's dependency for the baseline: it uses `childEnv('run')` and the `COULDNT_RUN` gap report). **Also blocked by pieces 3 and 4.** That is a breakdown choice, with this reason: the plan assigns the parent's docs and the final census to this last session (session D), and both describe and check the port and group-stop owners, so they cannot be written truthfully before those pieces land.

## Slice of the approved plan

**File:** `test/system/harness/baseline.js`, plus a `test:baseline` script in `package.json`.

* Usage: `npm run test:baseline [-- --tier unit|system|all] [--ref <ref>] [--out <file>]`, and `npm run test:baseline -- --against <a.json> <b.json>`.
* Make a `git worktree` **of** `main` (the local ref; `--ref` overrides) **inside the run root**, so the leak trap's allowed area contains it. Record the sha in the output. **Do not use** `copy-trees.js`: it copies uncommitted work. Run the chosen tier there with `childEnv('run')`. Afterwards run `git worktree remove` and then `git worktree prune` (deleting the run root alone leaves dangling `.git/worktrees` metadata).
* `node_modules`: symlink the checkout's, but only if `package-lock.json` is identical between `main` and the checkout. Otherwise report a `COULDNT_RUN` gap, with its fix, through `preflight` (`git` need).
* The `system` tier prints its Harbour line the way the runner does.
* **Output:** a JSON object keyed `<file> › <suite path> › <test>` (repeats get an occurrence index). Values are `pass | fail | skip | todo | cancelled | couldnt-run`. Keys are sorted. A header carries `ref`, `sha`, `tier` and `harbour`. Parse `node --test` reporter events, not the human text.
* `--against` prints the tests whose outcome differs and the tests present in only one file, and exits non-zero on any difference.
* **Implemented as approved (LIN-4224 close-out):** the plan-review corrections (reporter from the checkout, visible preload choice in the npm script, sha printed, origin/main warning) were all applied. One deviation: reporter events go to a run-root file opened by the baseline process instead of through `--test-reporter-destination`, because the tier's leak trap flags the path on a `/tmp`-rooted host. PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/321](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/321>), merged as `86bde97`. Full history is in the task snapshots and comment trail.

**Docs (**`docs/testing-and-ci.md`**,** `test/system/README.md`**):**

* Delete the hand-run baseline table and replace it with the one command.
* State which skip rule applies to which tier. Unit: host-precondition skips, as today. Heavy tier: a missing prerequisite is **not** a skip; it is `COULDNT_RUN`.
* Document the exit-code table, the pre-flight and the `Harbour: <dir> @ <sha>[ dirty]` line.
* Replace the "if the ports are busy, look for `node server.js` with PPID 1" advice, since ports are now assigned.

**Final census:** confirm that rules (a) leader-only and `kill(-`, (b) env and (c) ports are all present and run in `npm test`, that every allowlist entry has its reason, and that no stale entry remains. Then walk the parent's "At merge" list item by item.

## Testing strategy (witnesses)

* Build a fixture repo whose `main` has one failing and one passing test, and whose working tree has an uncommitted change. The output lists `main`'s outcomes, without the uncommitted change, and it is **byte-identical on a second run**.
* `--against` on two crafted outputs reports exactly the differing rows, plus the one-sided rows, and exits non-zero.
* After a run, `git worktree list` shows no leftover worktree.
* `npm test` is green, and `npm run test:baseline` runs end to end on this checkout.

## Acceptance

* Parent "Done when": **a scripted baseline**, one command whose output can be compared.
* The parent's "At merge" list holds, including the docs changes.
* This piece's PR, or a comment on LIN-4219, carries the parent's close-out: what changed · what was left and why · what still looks fuzzy · follow-ups listed (not filed), including every fixed-port registry entry and every census allowlist entry, each with its reason.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4219 — *simple-dispatcher: the heavy test tier stands on one harness*. The parent's description holds the full scope, the "Done when" and "At merge" lists, the layout table and the **Implementation Plan**. Its comment trail holds the approving `### Plan Review Verdict` (comment `4ea51c1c-fa0a-44b9-9a63-c614f8fd7f56`). Read both before starting.

**Starting point (discharged):** the parent's approved plan was followed; course changes were posted on LIN-4219.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4219's approving plan-review (comment 4ea51c1c-fa0a-44b9-9a63-c614f8fd7f56, rev 1; the verdict names no revision number, and this is the only plan revision and the only verdict on the trail)
Grounding commit: simple-dispatcher `main` @ `502901c` (plan and review both grounded here; re-checked at breakdown on 2026-11-04, and nothing under `test/`, `docs/testing-and-ci.md`, `package.json` or `e2e-smoke.js` has changed)

**Constraints from the parent (all pieces):** nothing new at the repo root. `signal-guard.js` and `protected-paths.js` stay untouched. Each piece is its own PR, with its own run of `npm test`, plus `test:system` / `test:mutation` where the piece touches them. Out of scope, for the parent's close-out to list (not file): a scheduled/CI heavy-tier run (LIN-3160), pinned Harbour per dispatcher commit, splitting `run-mutations.js`, a test-infra module map, `e2e-smoke.js` joining the tier, the shared source sandbox.

comments.body: LIN-4223 (heavy-tier harness 4/5) is merged: PR #317, `54febbf` on `main`. `stopGroup` / `stopGroupSync` / `groupAlive` / `KILL_GRACE_MS` and the group-record helpers now live in `test/system/harness/stop-group.js`; Harbour is spawned detached; the census is `test/harness-kill-census.test.js`. This unblocks LIN-4224. Note for the final census: the allowlist dropped `e2e-smoke.js:1721` (a comment, which the census skips). Details in the close-out comment on LIN-4223.

**Heads-up from LIN-4222 (merged, PR #320 / `3330526`):** `npm run test:system` is not green on `main` because of two known failures, tracked in LIN-4187 (`observation-feed`) and LIN-4188 (`tap1-openrouter`). They fail identically on clean `main`, so the scripted baseline should list them as known-red until those close. Port flakes in the heavy tier now surface as `Harbour exited before it became ready … EADDRINUSE` after 3 attempts, or as ECONNREFUSED in a system file; this baseline is the named monitor for them.

**Beat 1/4 done (local commit `0c70f78` on `feat/lin-4224-test-baseline`, not pushed yet):** the core of `npm run test:baseline`. It covers the worktree of `main` in the run root, the sha in the header, the origin/main warning, remove-then-prune cleanup (including on signal or crash), `childEnv('run')`, the checkout reporter, the event parser, sorted keys with occurrence indexes, and the lockfile gate.

Evidence:
- `npm test`: 4225 tests, 4220 pass, 0 fail, 5 skip (30 new).
- `npm run test:baseline` on `main` @ `3330526`: 4195 tests (4190 pass, 5 skip). Two runs are byte-identical (sha1 `bdf877dd…`), the same on a `/tmp`-rooted host, and leave no leftover worktree.
- `--tier system`: 142 pass, 2 known-red (LIN-4187, LIN-4188).

Every witness was seen red under a mutation first. Course changes are posted on LIN-4219.

Still to come: `--against`, docs, known-red listing, final census, PR.

**Beat 2/4 done (local commit `04ecb8a` on `feat/lin-4224-test-baseline`, not pushed):**

- `--against <saved>` (a fresh run compared with a saved report) and `--against <a> <b>` (two saved reports, no run).
- Exit 0 when identical, 1 on any difference, 75 when nothing or not everything was judged. 75 wins over 1.
- LIN-4187 and LIN-4188 are labelled known-red (by file, with reasons) but still count as differences.
- The header stays as approved, per the ruling on decision `lin4224-header-exits`. The "failure visible in no test row" gap is now in the code's LIMITS note and will be in the PR's follow-ups.

Results on this branch:
- `npm test`: 4245 tests, 4240 pass, 0 fail, 5 skip.
- `test:system`: 142 pass, 2 fail (`observation-feed`, `tap1-openrouter`), the same names as the system baseline of clean `main` @ `3330526`.
- `test:mutation`: 67/67 killed.

Every new witness was seen red under a mutation (A1–A9). The CLI was also run end to end on this checkout: identical reports exit 0, one flipped row exits 1, a fresh system run against the saved report exits 0, and a `/tmp` path is refused with 75.

**Beat 3/4 done (local commit `1b05a28`, not pushed): the docs.**

`docs/testing-and-ci.md`:
- The hand-run baseline table is replaced by `npm run test:baseline` (with `--against`, the known-red labels, the exit table, and the stderr-only limit).
- New: which skip rule applies to which tier (unit tier: skip with a reason; heavy tier: `COULDNT_RUN`).
- New: the heavy-tier exit codes, pre-flight, and the Harbour line.
- The "look for `node server.js` with PPID 1" advice is gone, replaced by the group-stop (LIN-4223) and assigned-port (LIN-4222) facts.

Also updated:
- `test/system/README.md`: prerequisites, exit 75, and the mutation-gate limit.
- `docs/full-system-test-plan.md`: a stale "give each file its own port" line.

Every quoted command, message and exit was run on this checkout. `npm test`: 4247 tests, 4242 pass, 0 fail (+2 are the doc-path resolver's cases for the new links). `npm run test:baseline`: `main` @ `3330526`, 4195 tests, 4190 pass, 5 skip, exit 0, no worktree left.

**LIN-4224: PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/321** (head `1b05a28`, 3 commits). Not merged, not Done: review and close-out own that.

**CI:** `gh pr checks 321` reports one check, `unit tests`, as **pass** (2m34s, run https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/actions/runs/41856163967/job/126665248102). It ran on Linux / node 22: 4233 tests, 4226 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped (macOS-only suites skip there).

**Verified at this head:**
- `npm test`: 4247 tests, 4242 pass, 0 fail, 5 skip, on node 25.9.0 and on node 22.21.0 (the CI version).
- `npm run test:system`: 142 pass, 2 fail (`observation-feed`, LIN-4187; `tap1-openrouter`, LIN-4188). These are identical by name to `npm run test:baseline -- --tier system` on clean `main` @ `3330526`.
- `npm run test:mutation`: 67/67 killed.
- `npm run test:baseline`: 4195 tests, 4190 pass, 5 skip, exit 0, byte-identical to earlier runs. `git worktree list` shows only the checkout, and `.git/worktrees` has 0 entries.
- `signal-guard.js` and `test/protected-paths.js` are untouched. Nothing new at the repo root.

### Final census

- (b) hand-built child env: `test/child-env-census.test.js`, with ceilings 27 entries / 42 sites, pinned by equality.
- (c) literal ports: `test/child-env-census.test.js` rule (c), with no allowlist; `test/ports-registry.test.js` checks the fixed-port registry.

Every allowlist entry has a reason, and stale entries fail. As a live check, a throwaway file with one violation of each rule made all four fire, naming lines 3, 4, 5 and 6. The file was deleted, and the censuses passed 60/60.

**The parent's "At merge" list:** all ✅.

| both summaries print the Harbour line | `test:system` and `test:mutation` print `Harbour: …/LinearViewer @ eb44eff9` |

**Fixed-port registry:** empty.

**Kill census (`test/harness-kill-census.test.js`), 6 entries**

  - a failure visible in no test row is stderr-only;

- Retire the KNOWN_RED entries when LIN-4187 and LIN-4188 close.

## Review — LIN-4224

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/321 at head `1b05a28` (3 commits on `main` @ `3330526`; local `main` = `origin/main`).

CI: green. The one check, `unit tests` (CI workflow, run 41856163967), passed on `1b05a28`. The heavy tier is not in CI, so I re-ran it myself (below).

### Scope vs plan
The diff touches only the planned places: `baseline.js` with its report and reporter modules under `test/system/harness/`, the `test:baseline` script, `docs/testing-and-ci.md`, `test/system/README.md`, and the tests. It also touches two small things outside that list, both stated:
- `run-system.js` now exports `SUITE_ARGS`, so the baseline reuses the runner's argv instead of copying it.
- One line in `docs/full-system-test-plan.md` said each file needs its own port, which was stale.

One course change from plan note 7: the reporter's events go to a run-root file that this process opens and passes to the tier as stdout, instead of through `--test-reporter-destination <path>`. The reason (the tier's leak trap flags the path on a `/tmp`-rooted host) is in the code and on LIN-4219. I accept it: the events still land in the run root, and the reporter still comes from the checkout by absolute path.

The preload choice is visible in the npm script: `node --require ./test/isolate-run.js test/system/harness/baseline.js`. `signal-guard.js` and `test/protected-paths.js` have no diff since `502901c`, and nothing new was added at the repo root.

### Regression check
`git log -- run-system.js package.json docs/testing-and-ci.md test/system/README.md` shows the LIN-4221/4222 commits and the earlier LIN-4180/4181/4077 work. Nothing that was reverted is re-applied. The `SUITE_ARGS` refactor keeps the same argv (the frozen array is spread into `spawn`). `npm run test:system` at head gives the same two failures as clean `main`.

### Evidence I re-ran myself (macOS, node 25.9)
- `npm test`: 4247 tests, 4242 pass, 0 fail, 5 skip.
- `npm run test:baseline -- --out …`: `main @ 3330526`, 4195 tests (4190 pass, 5 skip), exit 0. The sha1 is `bdf877dd…`, the same bytes as the author's runs. `git worktree list` shows only the checkout, and there is no `.git/worktrees` folder.
- `--tier system`: 144 tests, 142 pass, 2 fail, both labelled known-red (LIN-4187 `observation-feed`, LIN-4188 `tap1-openrouter`). Exit 0, and the header carries the `Harbour: …/LinearViewer @ eb44eff9` line.
- `--tier all`, which no test drives end to end: exit 0. Its tests are exactly the union of the unit and system reports (4339 keys).
- `npm run test:system` (through `run-system.js`, after the `SUITE_ARGS` refactor): 142 pass, 2 fail, the same two names.
- `--against a a`: `identical (144 tests)`, exit 0. Against a copy with one flipped row, one removed row and one added row, it printed exactly those 3 rows and exited 1.
- `HARBOUR_DIR=/nonexistent … --tier system`: `Missing harbour: …` with its fix, exit 75, no worktree made.

### Mutation checks (LIN-2274). Each one was reverted afterwards, and the tree is clean.
- Tier `cwd` set to the repo instead of the worktree (so uncommitted work leaks in): 3 red, including "reports main's outcomes, not the working tree's".
- Key sort dropped in `formatReport`: 3 red (the sort and byte-identity witnesses).
- Lockfile gate always passes: 1 red (the "package-lock.json that differs" gap).
- Origin-drift warning suppressed: 1 red.
- `againstExit` returns OK when there are differences: 5 red.
- `worktree remove` and `prune` both removed: 7 red (the cleanup, signal and crash witnesses).
- **`git worktree prune` alone removed: stays green (50/50).** On git 2.46, `git worktree remove --force` already deletes the `.git/worktrees` entry, even when the folder is already gone (I checked by hand). So prune is a fallback no test reaches. It is the planned order (remove, then prune), harmless, and I could not build a case on current git where prune is the only thing that cleans up. This is an observation, not a fix: no change requested.

### Isolated or a class?
I searched the `*.md` files for other hand-run baselines and for "PPID 1", "ports are busy" and "own port". There are none left: the only other "baseline" hit, in `docs/linux-substrate-findings.md`, is about memory. The `e2e-smoke.js` sibling is outside scope by the parent's own list. This change is isolated.

### Final census and close-out
I spot-checked the census against the tree:
- `test/system/mutation/run-mutations.js` no longer defines `stopGroup`, `groupAlive` or `killerEnvFor`.
- The three census and registry test files are present and green in `npm test`.
- The docs carry the skip rule for each tier, the exit table, the pre-flight and the Harbour line.

The PR body holds the parent's close-out: what changed, what was left and why, what still looks fuzzy, follow-ups (listed, not filed), the empty fixed-port registry, and every kill-census and env-census allowlist entry with its reason. That meets the acceptance item "PR or a comment on LIN-4219".

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **The heavy tier (`--tier system` and `--tier all` of the baseline, and `test:system` after the `SUITE_ARGS` refactor).** Inside: this is the baseline's own claim. CI runs only the unit tier. **Discharged** by my re-runs above at `1b05a28`: the expected result is 142 pass with exactly the two known-red names, exit 0, and no leftover worktree.
- **The `KNOWN_RED` labels for LIN-4187 and LIN-4188 going stale.** Inside: this ticket added the list. Settled by a **named monitor**. When either file runs without failing, the baseline prints `baseline: known-red <ticket> (<file>) did not fail here; if it is fixed on main, drop its KNOWN_RED entry` on stderr.
